e: A tour bus and a truck collide in Akhisar, killing 11 people and injuring 27 others.
PKK militants withdraw from four sites in northern Iraq as part of a peace initiative with Turkey.
Two people are killed and at least two more are trapped after a partial collapse of a seven-story building in Istanbul.
Eight girls are stabbed, one of them fatally, at a middle school in Istanbul.
The chair of the Turkish Football Federation's central referee board, Ferhat Gündoğdu, is detained along with six others as part of a police investigation into corruption.
A court in Istanbul sentences comedian Deniz Göktaş to just over 19 months imprisonment for "insulting" President Erdogan.
A 41-year-old man fatally shoots his uncle at a high school in Osmaniye.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu orders the drafting of an ICC case against President Erdogan, citing Turkey's alleged persecution of Kurdish minorities and the Turkish government's alleged financial assistance for Hamas.
Turkey agrees to gradually transfer Bashiqa base to Iraq.
A magnitude 5.4 earthquake hits Şanlıurfa Province, injuring 40 people.
Eleven students are injured in a school shooting in Turgutlu, Manisa Province.
Turkey revokes Bank Mellat's operating license amid the US-led economic isolation campaign against Iran.
Widespread raids are conducted on LGBTQ bars, activists’ houses and HIV support groups as part of a crackdown announced by President Erdoğan.

The US Treasury announces that it has cut off Turkish investment bank Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi and two subsidiaries from dollar transactions because of their dealings with the Iranian regime.
An international arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is issued by Turkey over the interception of the Gaza Freedom Flotilla.
An F-16 Fighting Falcon of the Turkish Air Force crashes in Yalova Province. The pilot ejects safely.
Turkey passes legislation providing thousands of PKK operatives a conditional amnesty once the PKK fully relinquishes its weapons.
Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey sign a joint defense agreement.
Iraq signs a one-year exportation agreement with Turkey to export 750 thousand barrels of petroleum through the Ceyhan pipeline.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Turkey, citing the presence of alleged forced labor in the supply chain.
A magnitude 5.0 earthquake hits Malatya Province, injuring 32 people.
A court in Istanbul imprisons comedian Deniz Göktaş for insulting President Erdoğan and religious principles.
At least 209 people are arrested in raids by security forces across Ankara ahead of the 2026 Ankara NATO summit.
The Turkish-flagged fishing boat Duru 67 is attacked and sunk in the Black Sea off Sevastopol, killing one sailor and injuring four others.
A bus crashes into highway barriers and catches fire in Denizli Province, killing eight people and injuring 33 others.
Three people are killed following floods in Hatay Province.
An appeals court in Ankara annuls the results of the CHP's 2023 congress, effectively removing Özgür Özel as party chairman in favor of Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake hits Malatya Province, injuring 74 people.
Six people are killed in a series of shootings carried out by the same person in Tarsus.
Turkey lifts restrictions on direct trade with Armenia.
Authorities arrest 324 suspects linked to Islamic State following operations in 47 provinces.
The European Court of Human Rights, in the case of Yasak v. Türkiye, rules that Article 7 and Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights had been violated.
Eight people are sentenced to up to 7.5 years' imprisonment for the plunging of a cable car on Tünek Tepe in 2024 that killed one person.
Twelve people are killed in a school shooting in Kahramanmaraş. The 14-year old perpetrator is also killed.
Sixteen people are injured in a school shooting in Siverek, Şanlıurfa Province. The 19-year old perpetrator dies by suicide.

Three gunmen open fire on police outside the building housing the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, resulting in a shootout that leaves one of the attackers dead and the other two injured. Two police officers are also injured.
One person is killed and 10 others are injured, including one critically, when a natural gas explosion collapses two residential buildings in Fatih, Istanbul.
Iraq reaches a deal with Turkey and the Kurdistan Region to resume oil exports through the Kirkuk–Ceyhan Oil Pipeline.
Turkey intercepts an Iranian ballistic missile violating its airspace.
A boat carrying migrants collides with a Turkish Coast Guard vessel off Demre, Antalya Province, killing 14 passengers.
